rule: Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings doctrine section coupling
description: `plugin/governance/remediation-doctrine.md` `## Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings` is the single source for how a user's rejection of a finding, and a threat model, persist across review runs. The source pin is the section heading. Four further pins in the same file carry the load-bearing claims. (1) The definition: a user's rejection of a finding and a threat model are decisions, each recorded at its source in the project's durable design records. (2) The key: the recorded decision, never a finding id or a question; rewriting the key back to a finding id or a per-run question turns the suite red. (3) The condition and its obligation in one span: a later finding that contests a recorded decision is a repeat, and the reviewer rejects it by citing the record, lists it for the user before the merge, does not fix it, and never asks again; deleting any one of those four obligations, or the before-the-merge timing, turns the suite red. The span names no surface: where the user sees a repeat, the PR body or a thread reply, is the consumers' text, unpinned here. The same span carries the boundary: a finding that shows a failure the record does not cover is new and gets First-Finding Triage. (4) The write obligation, its condition and its two writers in one span: a user's rejection is recorded before the next review reads it, by the reviewer that asked when the answer reaches it in the same run, the local reviewer in a delivery run and the GitHub reviewer in a PR watch, and otherwise by the next plan as a plan step; deleting the before-the-next-review timing, the same-run reviewer writer or the next-plan fallback turns the suite red. The consumers pin the POINTER only, never remedy prose, so honest rewording of the doctrine body does not break them: `plugin/agents/local-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/overlord.md` and `plugin/agents/cerebrate.md` must still cite the doctrine file with the section name `(Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings)`. What this pin honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in these five named files; it claims nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion that leaves the pinned bytes intact is invisible: surrounding prose that also lets a reviewer ask the user again, or that keys a decision on a finding id elsewhere, stays green; (2) the role-named destination and the branch-or-trunk clause are unpinned, so deleting either alone stays green; (3) the pin sees only the five files it names, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW reviewer that never points at the section at all, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.
